story: On a sunny Thursday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary is reading the bulletin board on Magnolia Loop to find out the Architectural Review filing deadlines for golf cart modifications, while Donna heads over to join him there. Hal sits on his porch with a cup of coffee, keeping an eye on the street and thinking ahead to Friday's dinner at Rosa's. Back in her kitchen, Rosa is planning the menu and making a list of what she needs to buy for the main dish and sides.
events: Gary (street bulletin board): Read the board for Architectural Review filing info and deadlines for cart modifications
Donna headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Hal waited: Sipping coffee on the porch, keeping a steady eye on Magnolia Loop and thinking about Friday's dinner at Rosa's.
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Plan Friday's menu and check what I need to buy for the main dish and sides

gary.thought_process: Cart's wired and I've got the ten o'clock cutoff timer built in, so the sound system is already L-03 friendly. The lights and speakers are visible from the street, though, so L-01 says I need Architectural Review approval before I install anything permanent. Hal offered to check my paperwork line by line, and I'm on Magnolia Loop, where the street bulletin board probably has the review submission notice or deadlines. I'm alone here, so nobody to talk to. Best move is to check the board for how to file and when review meets, then bring the draft to Hal.

parameters.content: Read the board for Architectural Review filing info and deadlines for cart modifications

donna.thought_process: Gary's paddle is out, the club calendar is penciled, and I already texted him last tick that his paddle is ready and asked for a time. No need to nag him again before he answers. Nobody's here to talk to, and I've got no unfinished business at the bag or calendar. Better to go be visible and social rather than sit by the phone. Magnolia Loop is where the neighbors are on a sunny Thursday morning, and I might bump into Gary or Rosa or Hal there and press the ladder plan in person.

parameters.content: Texts are sent and the paddle is ready, so I'm heading out onto Magnolia Loop to see who's about and catch Gary in person.

hal.thought_process: I've counted the flamingos, logged my tally, and Gary's paperwork looks in order, so the street is quiet and honest for now. I'm already settled on the porch with my coffee. Nobody is in line-of-sight, so there's nobody to talk to. The notebook entry is made, and I've nothing left to file this tick. Might as well enjoy a sunny November morning and keep an eye on Magnolia Loop. Friday dinner at Rosa's gives me something to look forward to.

parameters.content: Sipping coffee on the porch, keeping a steady eye on Magnolia Loop and thinking about Friday's dinner at Rosa's.

rosa.thought_process: I've already set out the good plates, counted chairs, and checked my shift schedule twice, so Thursday coffee and Friday night are covered. Nobody is nearby to talk to, and re-checking the schedule would just be repeating myself. Friday's dinner needs real food planning: Gary is bringing cornbread, so I should figure out the main dish and sides. The kitchen is the next useful step toward getting all three neighbors at my table.

parameters.content: Plan Friday's menu and check what I need to buy for the main dish and sides

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
